title: Scaffold the Next.js application and its production build/start primitives
statement: Create the application under `app/` and make `next build` followed by `next start` work on loopback, with a route that responds. No MDX integration of any kind is configured here. The documented one-command launcher is TSK-0013's.
notes: First because everything else needs somewhere to live. ⚠️ Production mode only (DEC-0018): `next dev` is a contributor workflow and never a shipped configuration, so the launch command must not offer it as an option. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-08-27 — A DISCARDED ARCHITECTURE HAD LEAKED IN. The original statement configured `@next/mdx`, an absolute remark-plugin path and Turbopack's config-serialisation constraint. All three belong to FILE-ROUTED MDX, which DEC-0020 explicitly rejected: AST-0030 measured that path compiling the document into the build so an edit changes nothing, which fails REQ-0018. ⚠️ HOW IT GOT IN IS WORTH RECORDING. Those settings came from the PROBE that measured the rejected option. The probe's incidental setup was carried into the plan as though it were the design — the measurement was right and the configuration it needed was the losing alternative's. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-27, and one thing was measured rather than chosen. The routes were first placed at `src/app/` to keep the shell clear of `app/server.mjs`, the walking skeleton DEC-0017 preserves. Next.js ignored them: a root `app/` directory takes precedence over `src/app/`, so the build reported `Route (pages)` with only `/404` and none of the authored files appeared. Moving them to `app/` produced `Route (app)` with `○ /`, and the skeleton is left alone as a colocated non-route file — `server.mjs` is not a `page`, `layout` or `route`, and `.mjs` is not in the default `pageExtensions`. ⚠️ A build that SUCCEEDS while rendering nothing you wrote is the failure mode worth remembering here: `✓ Compiled successfully` was printed both times, and only the route table said which files Next.js had actually found. ⚠️ VERIFIED FROM CLEAN: `.next` removed, `npm run shell:build` from scratch, `next start` bound to 127.0.0.1 only (confirmed against the listening socket, not assumed from the flag), HTTP 200 with the expected body, process terminated and the port confirmed free. `npm audit` reports zero vulnerabilities after adding next, react and react-dom. ⚠️ NOT DONE HERE, on purpose: no MDX integration of any kind, no watcher, no launcher that owns processes, and no planning-content read. The route reads nothing — a convenience read would be the first violation of REQ-0021's confinement, whose own enforcement (TSK-0006, TSK-0015) does not exist yet.
